rules.statement: When enforcing a collection-valued `*_supported` policy setting, treat it as restrict-only-if-present: read it with `TryGetValue` and reject only when it is present and does not contain the item, never with `GetValue`. The exception is an algorithm list that decides what the server accepts from another party: when unset, it permits nothing.
rules.why: Absence of a `*_supported` setting means no restriction, so extensions and custom scopes or grants aren't blocked. `GetValue` throws on an unset collection that has no default. ADR-0155 later made inbound algorithm-acceptance lists permit nothing when unset.
rules.check: Look for enforcement code that reads a `*_supported` setting with `GetValue`, or that rejects a request when the setting is missing. For an algorithm list governing what is accepted from another party, check instead that a missing list rejects everything.

rules.statement: Do not hardcode policy values for intersect-merged capability-list settings as setting-descriptor defaults; supply them through a replaceable baseline provider applied to the root layer before configuration, so hosts can extend, override or clear them.
rules.why: Intersect only narrows, so a hardcoded root default becomes a ceiling nobody can raise and blocks any extension that adds a capability. Capability belongs to the registries, and policy belongs to a layer the host can override.
rules.check: Look for new or changed `Default` values on collection settings merged with `Intersect` (for example `*_supported` lists) that are set as literals on the descriptor instead of in the baseline defaults provider.

rules.statement: In generic code constrained with `where T : notnull`, do not detect whether a value is present by testing a `T?` field or parameter against null; track presence with an explicit boolean flag, or constrain to `struct` and use a real `Nullable<T>`.
rules.why: Under a `notnull` constraint, `T?` on a value type is just `T`, not `Nullable<T>`, so it is never null. The null check always reports a value, and `default(T)` (for example `TimeSpan.Zero`) gets used by mistake.
rules.check: Look for generic types or methods with a `notnull` (or no) constraint that compute presence with `x is not null` or `x != null` on a `T?` and then use that result to decide whether a default or value exists.

rules.statement: A scalar setting with no default, where unset means no constraint, must stay absent when not configured; read it as an optional `Nullable<T>` and apply the constraint only when it has a value.
rules.why: Materializing `default(T)` for such a setting turns "no constraint" into a constraint of zero. For example, a zero max-age rejected every fresh login and returned `login_required` to `prompt=none` requests.
rules.check: Look for reads of optional scalar settings that fall back to `default(T)` or use a throwing getter instead of a try-get or nullable read. Also look for code that adds a default value to the effective settings for a descriptor that has none.
